source: Hypercar cooling system (car_hyper, car_hyper_n2o), sized from the heat load of its 5.1 L twin-turbo V8 (data/engine_thermal/hyper_v8_one1.json). The class passenger-car radiator (0.35 m2, UA 1500 W/K at 2.0 kg/s air) cannot carry it: at full power the engine puts about 3.06 MW of released fuel energy into the cylinders (measured on the final car by the diag in tests/unit/test_game_car_thermal.cpp at 427 km/h, 7636 rpm: 612 kW wall heat = wall_heat_fraction 0.20 [AS, class, pinned to the turbo configuration's 0.20] x 3.06 MW, plus 88 kW friction heat of which 30 % goes to the oil), against a design target in the brief of 2.5 MW fuel and 400-500 kW to the coolant; the class radiator with its own 0.35 ram coefficient reaches only about 4.6 kW/K at 427 km/h and would need 612/4.6 = 133 K above ambient, so the coolant passes the 118 C overheat warning within seconds of a full-throttle pull. Sizing [D]/[AS] (upsized 2026-10-16 after the owner's answer on PR #28: the setup check grades the time to the limit at constant full power, and the stock hypercar must be clean or at most a plain warning; the first version was critical, 118 C after 16 s from the warm start, steady 134.5 C): the class core is scaled by frontal area and core depth. A = 1.4 m2 [AS: three to four ducted cores - two side-pod/front cores of about 0.45 m2 and a tail core of about 0.5 m2; a 1500 hp mid-engine hypercar runs ten or more heat exchangers, of which the engine high-temperature circuit is the largest share, so 1.4 m2 of engine-coolant core is at the upper end but within that class], core_factor 1.2 [AS: a thicker multi-row brazed aluminium race core, 1.2x the heat exchange per area of the class passenger core at equal face velocity], so UA_ref = 1500 W/K x (1.4/0.35) x 1.2 = 7200 W/K at air_mass_flow_ref = 2.0 kg/s x (1.4/0.35) = 8.0 kg/s (the same 4.8 m/s face velocity as the class core), exponent 0.6 as the class [C, Incropera & DeWitt]. ram_coefficient 0.22 [AS]: face velocity = 0.22 x airspeed, ducted cores behind dedicated inlets and NACA/side ducts (the class 0.35 is an open sedan grille; 0.22 gives 26 m/s through the core at 427 km/h). Fan [AS]: 7.0 m/s face velocity (two or three high-flow brushless fans on the larger area; the class value is 3.5); on/off 98/93 C, warnings 118/50 C and the needle curve are the class values. oil_cooler.air_w_k_per_m_s 1.0 [AS]: a dedicated ducted air-oil cooler of about 1.0 W/K per m/s of airspeed (about 120 W/K at 427 km/h on top of the engine file's 1.27 W/K per m/s block-oil term). Setup check with these files (30 C day, the ram air the power holds, warm start; tests/unit/test_cooling_upgrades.cpp [.][cooling][long]): car_hyper coolant settles at 99.6 C, oil 120.4 C, neither limit reached: clean (race radiator + race oil cooler on top: 94.6 / 89.9 C). The cooling grades of data/cooling_systems/cooling_upgrades.json are factors on this stock size and still improve on it. The nitrous hypercar shares this file and is not sized for the shot: its check (the dyno sweep sprays without end) settles at 119.6 C coolant, reaches 118 C after 10 s from the warm start (critical) and the oil 135 C after 107 s, while a real shot lasts 35 s. Measured with these files (flat 40 km strip, assist auto-shift, warm start 91 C; tests/unit/test_game_car_thermal.cpp [.][diag][thermal_run] and test_cooling_upgrades.cpp [.][cooling][long]): full throttle from standstill at ISA 15 C peaks at 99.2 C coolant during the pull (about t = 15 s, before the thermostat has caught up), then the thermostat regulates 89-95 C on the 424 km/h plateau, oil 101.4 C after 170 s; on a 35 C day the pull peaks at 103.9 C (t = 20 s) and the 413 km/h plateau settles at 96.2 C coolant / 110.8 C oil after 170 s (the first sizing: 117.1 / 123.2 C), steady_thermal at that instant 96.2 C; with the race radiator and race oil cooler on top 93.9 / 89.3 C. The diag's nitrous run did not spray (the hyper sprays only in Sport drive mode), so the shot's temperatures with this size are not re-measured.
